dedupe_keys.name: noaa ncei space weather satellite anomalies archive

description: NOAA's National Centers for Environmental Information keeps an archive of records of satellite anomalies, compiled to understand and document how space weather affects spacecraft. It grew from the Satellite Anomaly Manager database begun by the former National Geophysical Data Center, into which operators and agencies from Australia, Canada, Germany, India, Japan, the United Kingdom and the United States contributed reports of malfunctions such as phantom commands, memory upsets, power losses and attitude control problems, together with the time and orbit so that they can be matched with geomagnetic storms, solar energetic particles and cosmic rays. Studies using it found seasonal and daily patterns in anomalies and links with geomagnetic and solar activity. The current page also offers anomaly data and analyses for particular spacecraft, including GOES-16 and GOES-17 and TDRS-1 for 1986 to 1993, and workshop material up to 2018. Coverage: many satellites, mainly from the 1970s to the 2010s. Format and access: Excel spreadsheets and PDF reports from NCEI, and a data.gov catalogue entry for the historical database, free. Caveats: contributions were voluntary and uneven, so the archive is not a census; the historical database is no longer updated and the page notes that NCEI is moving data to the cloud. Simulation uses: vulnerability of satellites and their services to space weather, fragility relationships between particle environment and anomaly rates, and scenario design for severe storms. Related records: the C-SWIMS inputs, Seradata and ESA-ADB cover other sides of satellite failures.
